messages:
Maria Chen: heads-up — ran into a cluster of 413s from the embeds route while testing the console payload suggestor. looks like suggestions are nudging clients to split, but clients hitting our quota router then get 413. can we align the UX and routing? :thinking:
Alex Gupta: ugh. can you paste a sample request/headers? thinking about whether the suggestor should return a preflight header that the client uses to split before send.
Maria Chen: here's the failing pattern:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client: internal-experiment
Body: { "inputs": [ ... huge array ... ] }
```

server logs: `413 payload too large -> route-splitter rejected`

We show a console bubble: "We recommend splitting this file into X chunks" but the client still POSTs the full array (got race/automation).
Chris Morales: Is the suggestor synchronous in the console flow or async? if it's async the client automation can POST before it sees the hint.
Maria Chen: current POC: suggestor runs on save -> writes a hint to the org-config + shows UI. it's not enforced.
Jing Li: From routing side: we have preflight header support (`X-Embed-Units-Estimate`) but almost nobody uses it. If the suggestor could inject a preflight header into the SDK proxied request (or offer a client-side snippet), we could avoid 413s and route accurately.
Sam Patel: we should be careful about trust model — routing uses estimate to pick route/quota, but we still validate size at ingress. estimates can be off and we'd need a rejection fallback path.
Alex Gupta: proposal: (1) console suggestor exposes a `suggest_split` API that returns an array of split offsets + an `estimated_units` value; (2) SDKs automatically prefer the split when receiving that response and set `X-Embed-Units-Estimate` when sending; (3) runtime falls back to async splitter if mismatch but rates limit the fallback.
Chris Morales: P1 question: how visible is this in billing/console? we need telemetry to tie 413s to suggestor decisions. otherwise support will be messy.
Maria Chen: agreed. we need a telemetry tag like `suggestor.v1` on preflight and a console dashboard card showing: suggestions shown vs accepted vs 413s.
Jing Li: telemetry detail: add a boolean field `suggestor_applied` and `suggestor_version` to the request trace. that can be an attribute in our traces/span tags.
Sam Patel: ops concern: if SDKs start auto-splitting silently, latency SLOs jump because of multiple RPCs. We need a cost/latency hint in the suggestor UI: "This split will increase end-to-end latency by ~40ms but reduce unit cost by 2.1x".
Alex Gupta: can the suggestor compute that? we have models for batching efficiency and average token length. even a coarse estimate is useful.
Maria Chen: yes — we already run a lightweight estimator that predicts batch hit rate and unit delta. it's not perfect but good for display.
Chris Morales: rollout plan: start with read-only suggestor + SDK opt-in that honors `suggest_split` responses. gate behind org flag and a small canary org set. console shows warning and a "apply split in SDK" code snippet instead of auto-enforcing.
Alex Gupta: ops telemetry: new metrics we need: `suggestor.shown.count`, `suggestor.accepted.count`, `ingress.413.count` tagged by `suggestor_version`, `preflight.header.present` and `preflight.vs.actual.discrepancy` histogram.
Jing Li: runtime: add a fast-path in router that if `X-Embed-Units-Estimate` present and within threshold, pick split-aware route. Otherwise fall back and attach `fallback_reason` tag.
Sam Patel: and add a debugging console link in the 413 response pointing to a support doc and the suggestor UI for that org. reduces triage time.
Maria Chen: UX ask: can the console show the estimated E2E latency and cost delta inline and a toggle "Include preflight header in SDK snippet"?
Chris Morales: yes. also we should add a nonblocking banner in the console: "We recommend splitting — click to insert split-snippet into your project". avoids automation races.
Alex Gupta: security: if SDK auto-inserts the header, we must ensure it can't be spoofed by arbitrary clients — authenticate and rate-limit preflight-estimates per API key.
Jing Li: agreed. we can bind estimate lifetimes to a short TTL and a signature HMAC using the org key to avoid stale/forged estimates.
Sam Patel: operational playbook: if preflight estimate mismatch > 20% for 1hr across 5% requests, alert to eng-platform. Add an automated rollout rollback if 413s increase by >50% in canary.
Maria Chen: sounds good. next steps: I'll draft a console PR that surfaces cost/latency deltas + a suggest API. Jing, can you prototype header consumer in router? Alex, can you draft telemetry metrics and dashboard mock?
Jing Li: I can do a small runtime patch, will test with local preflight toggles. ETA 3 days.
Alex Gupta: I'll sketch the grafana panels and alert rules. ETA 2 days.
Sam Patel: I'll write the support doc and 413 response link. ETA 1 day.

Maria Chen: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow after initial canary run. :thumbsup:
